ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the founder, all UBOs identified at/above the 25% threshold, authorized signatories, and counterparties against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the domestic watchlists of the Panamanian Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies to Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates as defined by Ley 23 de 2015; negative news and adverse media checks are required for every UBO before the foundation charter is executed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Sede Electrónica del Registro Público de Panamá (e-Registry platform of the Public Registry of Panama); official name clearance certificate: 'Vista Fiscal' (Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be submitted in Spanish or in Latin-script transliteration of a foreign name; Panama uses the Latin alphabet and does not require local-script transliteration, but names must be grammatically consistent with Spanish naming norms and must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing entity recorded in the Public Registry; a foundation name must include the words 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or its unmistakable Spanish designation, which cannot be replaced by a foreign-language equivalent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Vista Fiscal is rejected, the applicant or its registered agent may file a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' with the Dirección General del Registro Público within five (5) business days of the issuance of the official rejection notice under Ley 38 de 2000 and the internal registry procedures; alternatively, the applicant may immediately submit a new name application with a corrected distinct corporate name. The Vista Fiscal is renewable for successive thirty-day periods upon payment of the current statutory tariff before the filing of the incorporation deed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible for a non-licensed low-risk trading entity: the Private Interest Foundation must maintain a registered office in Panama at the physical address of a licensed registered agent ('agente residente'); a virtual or serviced office is accepted only insofar as it includes the registered agent's street address, dedicated mail forwarding, and custody of the statutory records; no in-country employees or operational facility are required on site for bulk dehydrated vegetables and spices trading through SWIFT LC and TT wire payments.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 10-15% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk, non-licensed commercial trading foundation; likelihood increases to a moderate-high range if the foundation is linked to UBOs of sanctioned/PEP status, adverse financial intelligence reports, or if the foundation holds significant inventory documentation without supporting commercial substance records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Régimen Jurídico de las Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended by Ley 2 de 2013 and Ley 52 de 2013, including the provisions on foundation charter contents, initial endowment, foundation council, protector, resident-agent obligation, and the mandatory registration with the Registro Público de Panamá conferring juridical personality; subsidiary application of the principles of the Ley General de Sociedades and the Codificación Registral where not contrary to the PIF regime.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Sede Central, Panama City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Carta Fundacional otorgada en Escritura Pública (Foundation Charter granted by public deed before a Panamanian Notary Public)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is fixed by Law 25 of 1995; the foundation charter must declare an initial endowment (commonly USD 100–USD 10,000) which may be in cash or in kind; no escrow deposit or bank certification of the endowment is required at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [FOUNDATION NAME] (FOUNDATION COUNCIL) – RESOLVED: 1. The initial endowment declared in the Foundation Charter is ratified and assigned. 2. The registered office shall be the address of the resident agent in Panama. 3. The Founding Council is constituted; the Founder is appointed President; [Name] is appointed Secretary and Protector. 4. The President and Secretary are authorized to open bank accounts with SWIFT/TT rails and to execute export contracts for dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper. 5. The Council is authorized to retain counsel, file the municipal operation notice, obtain sanitary and environmental permits, and register the Foundation for tax purposes. Adopted unanimously in the Republic of Panama on [date].

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; official e-portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (Sede Electrónica DGI/RUC Management).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF) obtains its statutory tax identifier (RUC, Registro Único de Contribuyentes) through the following procedural sequence: (1) Appoint a resident agent in Panama and duly register the PIF with the Registro Público de Panamá under Law 25 of 1995; (2) Submit a notarized and apostilled copy of the Foundation Charter and Regulations, together with an authentic copy of the initial council members' appointment; (3) Appear before DGI, physically or through the resident agent, to complete the Registro Único de Contribuyentes application, specifying the economic activity under ISIC 4638 (wholesale of dehydrated vegetables and spices); (4) Provide proof of the local registered office address (Paz y Salvo municipal or lease deed) and a sworn declaration of commencement of operations or of inactive status if no Panama-source revenue is expected; (5) Upon approval, DGI issues the RUC certificate with assigned tax obligations, including ITBMS registration and electronic invoicing categories. Where the PIF only earns foreign-source export revenue, DGI will normally issue an RUC without mandatory minimum monthly advance income tax payments, and the PIF remains eligible to invoice exports at 0% ITBMS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — Panama applies a pure territorial income tax system. A PIF is ordinarily tax-transparent for accumulated assets and beneficiary distributions, and it is taxable only on income derived from sources within Panama. Export trading income from dehydrated vegetables and spices, where title passes and delivery occurs abroad, is outside the Panamanian income tax base, so the entity level captures only Panama-source commercial revenue, rentals of local property, or certain locally rendered services. The PIF is not a typical pass-through under US check-the-box concepts; rather, its distributions are generally excluded from beneficiary taxation except where the underlying fund has realized taxable Panama-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not offer a US check-the-box election or a hybrid-mismatch election. However, the PIF may rely on the Law 25 of 1995 structure to ensure non-taxability of foreign-source trading income: (a) it may elect to remain a purely patrimonial entity by avoiding any resident agent activity that generates Panama-source profit; (b) if it becomes commercially active, it may elect the simplified Small Taxpayer (Pequeño Contribuyente) regime under the Código Fiscal, subject to the statutory gross turnover ceiling; and (c) for indirect tax purposes, it may elect to file ITBMS returns and claim export zero-rating rather than applying the optional VAT withholding mechanism for unregistered suppliers. No hybrid mismatch election mechanism exists in the Panamanian domestic code.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), a VAT-type consumption tax governed by the Código Fiscal and DGI regulations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Registration is mandatory for any natural or legal person habitually performing taxable transfers of goods or services in Panama, with no general turnover exemption for commercial exporters; the optional simplified Small Taxpayer (Pequeño Contribuyente) regime is available for gross annual taxable turnover of up to USD 300,000, while standard ITBMS registration and monthly filing apply above that threshold. A PIF exporting dehydrated vegetables and spices must register for ITBMS once it holds an RUC and issues any invoice, including zero-rated export invoices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has phased in mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) through DGI Resolution No. 202-4254 and complementary norms. Taxpayers with RUC active status must emit invoices through the DGI-authorised electronic platform, using a qualified electronic signature (Firma Electrónica), generating XML files, and transmitting them to DGI's fiscal clearance service. Exports and dispatch invoices must be electronically cleared with the customs code (SIGA, Sistema Integrado de Gestión Aduanera) and must include the 0% ITBMS flag. No physical fiscal printer stamping is required for export-documented commercial invoices, but all invoice serial numbers must be reported in the DGI e-factura control system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the export of tangible goods, including dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper, where the sale is made to a non-resident purchaser, the goods physically leave Panamanian territory, and the export is evidenced by an accepted customs declaration and transport document. Offshore services delivered to non-residents and effectively used outside Panama may also be zero-rated. The PIF must hold a valid RUC, record the transaction in the ITBMS return, and retain an unbroken evidence chain demonstrating delivery to the foreign buyer and receipt of payment from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación via SIGA with accepted estatus)
Commercial Invoice issued under e-factura showing 0% ITBMS and ISIC 4638 classification
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing physical exit from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/related bank credit advice evidencing payment received from the non-resident buyer
Certificate of Origin (optional but recommended for tariff benefit and audit substantiation)
Packing List and weight or crop inspection certificate for dehydrated vegetable products
Copy of the Fumigation or Phytosanitary Certificate where required by destination country
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI scrutinizes zero-rated export claims through documentary verification, cross-referencing customs e-exits (SIGA) against bank remittance evidence. Claimed zero-rating without a valid customs export declaration, clean transport document, or an actual foreign payment may be reassessed at the 7% ITBMS headline rate, with monthly surcharges of 5%, interest, and fines under Código Fiscal Articles 736-789. Artificially structured or simulated exports attract a punitive fine of up to 200% of the omitted tax and may be referred to the Fiscal Crimes jurisdiction for fraud. Unpaid ITBMS creates an automatic preferential claim of the DGI against the foundation's assets and, where the foundation has made irregular distributions to beneficiaries, retrospective clawback liability may extend to the distributees.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No traditional central bank exists in Panama. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) serves as the primary banking and financial regulatory authority; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal and clearing agent for the State. The U.S. Dollar is the sole legal tender and circulating currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full currency convertibility is statutory and de facto. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible into USD with no exchange-control restrictions. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, and repatriation of capital from a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) are not subject to prior authorization, conversion taxes, or mandatory custody requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters, including trading entities operating through a PIF, retain proceeds in their designated bank accounts in any permissible currency, subject only to documentary retention required under AML/CFT rules.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) without a Panama banking license or an express SBP-recognized foreign license cannot legally onboard a Panamanian PIF as a payment client. Only locally licensed banks, in association with SBP-regulated payment gateways, may lawfully hold funds or execute clearing transactions in Panama. Use of unlicensed EMIs would trigger adverse AML classification and potential fund seizure risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the foundation's authorized signers and/or the registered agent is generally mandatory for final account activation, particularly for non-resident PIF clients. Remote documentary opening is possible but requires notarized and apostilled foundation instruments, passport copies, and a live video interview with compliance officers; exceptions are at the bank's discretion and rarely granted for initial onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: PIF with bearer shares, non-disclosed beneficiaries, or foundation council with no independent beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Foundation Charter and Private Regulations (when applicable), certificate of good standing from the Public Registry of Panama, declaration of beneficiaries, sworn affidavit of source of funds, and current notarized identification for each disclosed beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore structure without local economic substance despite performing export sales in Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement in Panama for physical office, employee payroll records, inventory/purchase and sale contracts, logistics documents (B/L, invoices, packing lists), and a substance memorandum prepared by local counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparty or inconsistent trade volumes for dehydrated spices in export transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade financing documents: signed master sales agreement, purchase orders, bills of lading, commercial invoices, customs declarations from origin and destination, quality certificates, and a profit-margin reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual anticipated transaction patterns or use of layered intercompany payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business rationale, flow chart of the transaction structure, and audited financial statements of affiliated companies; bank may require a compliance opinion from a licensed outside AML expert.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from shareholders or external lenders are executed exclusively via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wire transfers with the stated purpose code 'Direct investment in a commercial enterprise' (e.g., investment in international trade). The bank will require the foundation to furnish a board resolution authorizing the investment, a clear explanation of the project (bulk dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper export), and source-of-funds documentation (shareholder bank statement, audited financials, or notarized loan agreement). Funds must be received in a designated capital escrow account or operational account in Panama before disbursement to trading counterparties.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are cleared through (i) standard TT wires via SWIFT MT103 for prepayments, open account, and documentary collections; and (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) opened through a Panama commercial bank for larger or fixture transactions. Documentary LC (MT700/MT707) is the preferred rail when the exporter of dehydrated spices requires guaranteed payment against presentation of compliant shipping documents. Bank payment terms are instructed under UCP 600 rules; settlement is effected in USD without local FX conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards against USD for EUR, CNY, and major trade currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for offshore currency exposures where the counterparty bank does not require physical delivery
Cross-currency swaps (USD vs. EUR or USD vs. CNY) available through international trading desks at licensed Panamanian banks
FX options (European-style) for hedging trade-related receivables and payables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Franchise Tax (Tasa Única) – Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues statutory interest and a surcharge; continued non-payment for three consecutive years may lead to administrative strike-off and loss of juridical personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end; generally 31 March for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines for late or non-filing, statutory interest on unpaid tax, and possible tax foreclosure proceedings against the foundation's assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Ownership (Law 23 of 2015)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Beneficiarios Finales – Dirección General de Ingresos / Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before 30 April, and within 30 days after any beneficial ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines are imposed for failure to register or update beneficial ownership; persistent non-compliance may result in restrictions on legal standing and contractual capacity in Panama.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Renewal Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the annual anniversary date of the foundation's registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a registered agent in Panama permits intervention by the Public Registry and may ultimately lead to cancellation of the foundation's registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required for a Private Interest Foundation engaged in commercial activities in Panama or when annual gross income exceeds the statutory threshold, typically USD 1,000,000; otherwise no statutory audit is required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB; Panama currently adopts IFRS/NIIF for financial reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Panama Law 23 of 2015, the foundation must identify natural persons who directly or indirectly own more than 25% of rights, control the foundation, or act as beneficial owners. Annual confirmation is due before 30 April, and any transfer of beneficial interest must be recorded and reported within 30 days of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of the Foundation Council

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial scope: Panama-source income is taxed at 25%, while foreign-source trading profits are exempt, yielding a 0% effective rate for export trading conducted outside Panama. Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) under Law 25 of 1995 are tax-neutral as to foundation assets, foreign bank accounts and foreign-source flows. No general statutory tax holiday applies to wholesale dehydrated food/spice trading under ISIC 4638.
